You may re-verify anything below yourself via Read/Grep/Glob/Bash — the diff is real and currently sitting uncommitted in the working tree at overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx. Do not just trust this summary if you want to check something directly.

## The plan step

Add a per-attribute render slot to overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx — the ONLY file this step may touch. Five changes: (1) new optional prop `renderVariationAttribute?: (attr: SfccVariationAttribute) => React.ReactNode` on `ProductViewProps`, with JSDoc documenting that the call site's `??` treats only `undefined` as absent — a returned `null` also falls through and is NOT a way to render nothing; (2) the existing inline per-attribute render body extracted VERBATIM into a new function `renderDefaultVariationAttribute(attr)` declared inside the component (closes over `intl`/`onVariationChange`); (3) no default value at the destructure point for the new prop; (4) call site becomes `variationAttributes.map((attr) => <React.Fragment key={attr.id}>{renderVariationAttribute?.(attr) ?? renderDefaultVariationAttribute(attr)}</React.Fragment>)`; (5) the file's header doc-comment corrected to name both `renderHeader` and `renderVariationAttribute` instead of claiming only one additive prop exists. This step is meant to be a pure, behaviour-preserving refactor — no caller anywhere yet passes the new prop (that's Step 4), so the fallback always fires and rendered output must be unchanged.

Plan's stated pass criteria: tsc/lint/test all exit 0 · diff shows exactly one file · changed lines < 90 · zero changes outside the four/five named regions (no reformatting, no comment deletion, no type tightening) · backgroundColor={name.toLowerCase()} still present exactly once with its audit-allow comment · grep -c 'exactly one additive optional prop' → 0 · grep -rn "renderVariationAttribute" node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/ → no hits · audit:tokens still reports exactly 4 unacknowledged / 22 acknowledged.

Baselines on this branch before this step (non-zero is not a failure you introduced): tsc = 0 errors. test = 26 files / 408 tests, all passing. lint = 20 problems (4 errors, 16 warnings), exit 1 — the 4 errors are pre-existing prettier/prettier issues in overrides/app/routes.tsx:23,24 and overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts:116,335, neither file in this diff. audit:tokens = exactly 4 unacknowledged (all in header/index.tsx and theme/components/{header.ts,navConstants.ts} — none in product-view) + 22 acknowledged, exit 1.

## Orchestrator's verdict (already run, independently verified — not just asserted)

**IN SCOPE.** One file, matches the manifest exactly. All 5 changes present and correctly implemented, confirmed by reading the actual diff hunks, not by trusting a description. tsc exit 0, test exit 0, file itself has zero lint errors (only 7 pre-existing warnings, unchanged in kind/count, shifted in line number only). Second audit-allow comment (index.jsx:754, a different guard than the one this step's block carries) confirmed untouched — appears as an unmodified context line in the diff. No import lines changed anywhere (`React.Fragment` resolves via the existing default `React` import).

On the "<90 changed lines" criterion: it fails literally — actual is 165 (git diff --stat: 93 insertions/72 deletions) to 167 (grep -c '^[-+]', includes the two diff-header lines). The Orchestrator adjudicated this itself (not by trusting the implementer) by stripping whitespace/indentation from both the removed block and the added function and content-diffing them directly, and by cross-checking ESLint warning line/column positions before vs. after in an isolated worktree. Conclusion: the entire excess is `git diff`'s lack of move-detection — extracting a ~60-line block into a new function unavoidably shows once as a full deletion and once as a near-identical full addition in a plain unified diff, roughly doubling that block's own line count regardless of how faithful the extraction is. No unrelated content, no drift, nothing hidden was found anywhere in the diff.

## Tester's findings (already run, independently re-verified all four gates itself rather than trusting the implementer's report — caught and corrected its own tee-pipe exit-code bug mid-run before reporting)

**Gates:** tsc 0/clean · lint exit 1, 20/4/16, exact match, zero new warnings, the 7 file-local warnings traced individually and confirmed pre-existing (moved, not new) · test 408/408 exit 0 · audit:tokens exactly 4 unacknowledged/22 acknowledged, the file's own acknowledged entries traced individually and confirmed pre-existing (moved, not new).

**Verbatim-extraction check:** confirmed via anchor-verified line-by-line manual read of the exact original range (baseline lines 786-846) against the exact new range (lines 706-764) — every JSX prop, expression, and the full 8-line "mimic native radio input" comment match character-for-character. Only three differences, all mechanically required by the extraction itself: the destructure moved from the map-callback parameter list into a `const {...} = attr;` statement inside the function body; one `values.map((...) => {` call collapsed from 2 source lines to 1 (pure Prettier reflow at the new, shallower indent depth); the closing syntax differs because a `.map()` callback close differs from a function-declaration close. Tester's own tokenizer script produced two spurious diffs and it caught and disclosed that as its own artifact rather than let it stand, relying on the direct line-read instead.

**backgroundColor={name.toLowerCase()}:** confirmed exactly one occurrence, line 715, unchanged. **Both relevant audit-allow comments** (index.jsx:689 at line 707, index.jsx:754 at line 871) confirmed present and still attached to the same lines/logic they guarded before; a third (index.jsx:636-638) found in passing, also untouched.

**JSDoc clarity on the null-vs-undefined trap:** confirmed clear in prose, not just implied by the code — states plainly that `null` also falls through and is not a way to render nothing, and names the correct alternative.

**Nested-key investigation** (`<React.Fragment key={attr.id}>` wrapping `<SwatchGroup key={id}>`): investigated, not guessed — confirmed react/jsx-key is actually active in this project's lint config (traced the actual config chain) and produces zero warnings on either line; confirmed via React reconciliation semantics that the two keys operate in non-overlapping scopes (the Fragment keys the list produced by .map(), the SwatchGroup key is inert since it has no siblings at that position); confirmed this exact redundancy already existed in the base file's original code (the base always put key={id} on this SwatchGroup when it was the direct .map() return) — the extraction didn't introduce it, just relocated it next to a second, harmless key.

**Two 🟡 should-fix findings, both judged NOT to block this step:**
1. `overrides/app/components/product-view/` has ZERO test/story coverage — no `.stories.tsx`, no `.test.ts(x)` anywhere, confirmed by directory listing and a repo-wide grep. This predates this diff entirely (this step adds no new file and was never scoped to add one) — but this step does add a second render-prop escape hatch with real `??`-fallback branching to an already-uncovered ~1000-line component. Tester marked this CONFIRMED / UNIFORM (will recur, worse, once Step 4 puts real logic behind this exact prop with still no harness).
2. The plan's own "<90 changed lines" criterion is judged unachievable for a correct execution of the exact refactor the plan itself specified — CONFIRMED via the exact literal method the plan names (167, or 164 excluding diff-header lines) — Tester frames this as a defect in the plan's criterion-writing, not in the code, and flags it as UNIFORM risk for any future step that extracts a same-file block of comparable size.

**🔵 notes, not blocking:** the audit-allow comment's line-citation (index.jsx:689) is slightly imprecise against the actual base file (off by ~4 lines) — pre-existing, not introduced or worsened by this diff. The new prop's TypeScript signature still permits `null` at the type level (the JSDoc guard is documentation-only, not compiler-enforced) — a thought for whoever wires a real caller in a later step, not a defect here. Base package call sites already pass several untyped extra props (`isLoading`, `showReviews`, `showVariationAttributes`) that don't exist on `ProductViewProps` at all — pre-existing, unrelated, flagged only for awareness.

**What Tester could not verify:** did not mount the component in a real render to directly observe (vs. reason about) the nested-key behaviour at runtime — no test/story harness exists to build on, and constructing one was judged disproportionate to this single reasoning-level question. Did not run Storybook or Playwright (no story exists for this component). Has no visibility into Steps 2-4, which don't exist on this branch yet, so cannot speak to whether the null-vs-undefined contract will actually be respected once real logic is wired up later.

## Your job

Score this step against your six axes (Pass criteria / Correctness / Design fidelity / Conformance / Completeness / Restraint) and return PASS or REWORK, per your own standard format. Two things I want your own independent judgement on, not a rubber stamp of the above:

1. Does the "<90 lines" criterion failing in a way both independent checks attribute entirely to git's lack of move-detection (verified by two different methods: whitespace-stripped content diff + ESLint warning position cross-check) count as the Pass-criteria axis failing, or as that specific sub-criterion being satisfied in spirit and the literal number being a flawed measure for this kind of change? Make the call yourself.

2. Design fidelity: this step changes zero rendered output (no caller passes the new prop yet, so the base render path always fires) — is that itself sufficient to consider Design fidelity PASSED for this step, or does it stay UNVERIFIED until Marcel's visual checkpoint regardless? State which, and why, per your own axis definition.

Also state plainly whether the two 🟡 findings (pre-existing test/story coverage gap; the criterion-measurement issue) should be carried forward as informational items for Marcel/PostBuild rather than treated as reasons to REWORK a step that was never scoped to add test coverage for the whole file.
